reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is physically sound: low-temperature annealing below Tg is a well-known method to relax quenched-in stresses and enhance short/medium-range order in metallic glasses, which can improve thermal stability, though the claim of also improving glass-forming ability (a property of the liquid) via a post-quench treatment is conceptually problematic.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, using standard DSC, XRD, and TEM to compare annealed vs. as-quenched samples, with a well-defined falsification criterion based on crystallization onset temperature and amorphous structure retention.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a practical post-processing route to enhance amorphous stability in P-containing HEAs, which is moderately useful, but the confusion between improving glass-forming ability (a liquid property) and stabilizing the existing glass limits its direct relevance to the research question.
